subject: Provenance lifecycle annex + subprocessor residency questions
messages:
From: Rosa Mendez <rosa.mendez@healthnova.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provenance lifecycle annex + subprocessor residency questions

Hi Jordan / Kimberly,

Thanks for the initial call earlier. Two follow-ups from our legal and security teams after reviewing the draft DPA:

- They want a short annex that describes the "provenance lifecycle" for PII that flows into your LLM ingest pipeline (what touches it, who has keys, where it is persisted and for how long). High level is fine but it should explicitly name any subprocessors that receive raw identifiers.
- We have an EU residency requirement for a subset of patient identifiers. We need to know whether any of your edge subprocessors perform tokenization or enrichment in EU regions (HealthNova requires either onshore processing or explicit subprocessor residency commitments).

Could you send a short annex + a data map (even a Drawio diagram) and confirm the residency posture for the edge vendors you use for enrichment?

We'd like the annex by next Friday (2027-04-16) if possible; Gabe will own the internal review.

Best,
Rosa

--
Rosa Mendez
Director, Security & Privacy
HealthNova

[Attachment: request_summary.xlsx (XLSX, 14KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rosa Mendez <rosa.mendez@healthnova.com>, Gabe Turner <gabe.turner@healthnova.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provenance lifecycle annex + subprocessor residency questions

Rosa / Gabe — thanks for the note and the clear asks.

Quick status and plan:
1) I attached a short annex (v2) that outlines the provenance lifecycle for PII through our standard ingest and LLM feature pipeline. It includes: ingest point, transient KV cache, persistent telemetry (redacted), model input path, enrichment subprocessors, and retention windows.

2) I also attached the ingest data map (Drawio export). The annex flags which subprocessors may see unredacted identifiers during enrichment and when we apply tokenization.

3) Residency posture: Most of our enrichment partners support region-aware deployment. For the handful that do not commit to EU-only processing by default, we have two options we can propose in the annex: (A) onshore processing via dedicated EU deployment, or (B) replace with an EU-resident subprocessor we already validated.

Marissa — can you review the annex and the subprocessor table for any accuracy changes on the listed edge vendors and KMS custody notes? I marked the items I want you to confirm with a FIXME comment in the draft.

Kimberly — looping you for legal redline preference (annex vs. DPA clause). If legal wants it in the main DPA we can push a small clause instead; otherwise annex is faster.

Rosa/Gabe — draft attached for your review; the source Drawio and a short comment list are in the Drive link below. If that works, we can aim for a final by 2027-04-15 to give HealthNova time to circulate.

Thanks,
Jordan
Senior Manager, GTM Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: provenance_annex_draft_v2.pdf (PDF, 132KB)]
[Attachment: ingest_data_map_v3.drawio (DRAWIO, 90KB)]

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cProvenanceDraft

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Provenance lifecycle annex + subprocessor residency questions

Jordan / Kimberly — reviewed the draft and left inline comments in the PDF (summary below). I did not send externally yet; want to confirm these before we share with HealthNova.

Summary of comments / asks:
- Table S1 (subprocessors): I flagged two vendors (EdgeEnrich LLC and Tokenix Ltd) where our field teams reported intermittent EU-only deployments. We need explicit confirmation from those vendors (I put a note to request their SAAS tenancy/residency docs).
- KMS custody: Annex currently states key custody is with Redwood KMS and customer-managed keys are supported. Please add the supported KMS providers for EU (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) and an explanation of what we mean by "customer-managed" (bring-your-own-key via a managed HSM vs. full key escrow).
- Retention timing: We should make the retention buckets more concrete (raw identifiers: 0-7 days ephemeral, enriched tokens: 30 days, telemetry: 365 days). Legal may push for shorter telemetry retention; noted.

I'll fetch the vendor residency confirmations over the next 48 hours and update the annex. For now I replaced FIXME with bracketed notes so you can see what still needs confirmation.

Marissa
Director, Product Compliance
Redwood Inference

[Quoted text]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Rosa Mendez <rosa.mendez@healthnova.com>, Gabe Turner <gabe.turner@healthnova.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Provenance lifecycle annex (answers + next steps)

Rosa / Gabe — attaching the updated annex and a short response matrix that addresses the three asks from your legal/security teams. Key points: 

- Subprocessor residency: EdgeEnrich LLC confirmed EU tenancy for the HealthNova workload (we have their tenancy attestations attached). Tokenix Ltd currently runs mixed tenancy; we offered two mitigation options and HealthNova can pick one in the annex: (1) Tokenix run only in EU for HealthNova via a dedicated tenant, or (2) replace Tokenix with Tokenix-EU (a sister company we validated).
- KMS custody: Annex now lists supported KMS providers (AWS KMS [CloudHSM], Azure Key Vault [HSM], Google Cloud KMS [HSM]) and clarifies BYOK is supported via an HSM-managed key with only us having ephemeral wrapping keys in runtime. The customer retains root key control when they supply it.
- Retention and retention windows: I updated the exact buckets to the concrete values Marissa suggested (raw identifiers: ephemeral 0-7 days; enriched tokens: 30 days; telemetry: 365 days). We added an option for a reduced telemetry window in the DPA if HealthNova requires shorter retention.

Next steps / timeline:
- Action (HealthNova): Confirm preferred mitigation for Tokenix by 2027-04-15.
- Action (Redwood): On receipt, we'll issue final annex and a DPA redline (if you prefer clause vs annex) by 2027-04-18.

Attachments: provenance_annex_draft_v2.pdf (updated with Marissa notes), ingest_data_map_v3.drawio export, EdgeEnrich_EU_attestation.pdf, Tokenix_residency_statement.pdf.

If you want, we can schedule a quick 30-min walkthrough next week to go through the annex and the data map.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, GTM Compliance
Redwood Inference
